newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU agree to postpone key decision on reform.
newsitem.headline: EU agree to postpone key decision on reform.

text.p: European Union leaders agreed on Tuesday to postpone a key decision on institutional reform until the 15-nation bloc is enlarged to take in new, east European members early next century, officials said. The decision on changing the weighted majority voting system was postponed after a deadlock between big countries seeking more votes to reflect their population, and small states clinging to historic over-representation.
"There is an agreement on the institutions, in the sense that they (member states) will decide what to do at the moment of enlargement," a senior EU official said.

The accord reached shortly before midnight (2200 GMT) on the second day of a summit appeared to clear the way for the adoption of a revised Maastricht treaty on European union, incorporating new powers on police, immigration, foreign policy and defence.
However, the foreign and defence sections were watered down at Britain's insistence, and Britain, Ireland and Denmark were all given opt-outs from the lifting of border controls.
